title: Experience Schema
description: What happens when a specific Actor goes through a specific Mission. The Experience is the persona-specific view — carrying thoughts, emotions, and barriers as experienced by this actor. It references a Mission for structure and an Actor for identity. An Experience can be rendered as a linear journey for communication.

title.description: Human-readable title (e.g., 'Sarah Martinez — Clothes Shopping Experience')

summary.description: Narrative summary of this actor's experience through the mission

references.description: Links to the Actor and Mission this Experience is derived from

contextRef.description: Which of the actor's contexts applies (e.g., ctx-working-mom-consumer)

path.description: The specific route this actor takes through the mission graph

nodeSequence.description: Ordered list of mission node IDs this actor visits

lanes.description: Declares which persona-specific data layers this experience tracks. Core typed lanes (emotions, barriers) have schema-validated structure. Extended lanes (needs, pain, persona-specific observations) use simple types. Inherits the mission's lane declarations for service-level lanes; adds persona-specific ones here.

nodes.description: Persona-specific content for each node in the path. Each entry references a mission node and adds the actor's thoughts, emotions, barriers, needs, pains, and other lane content.

nodeRef.description: Reference to a node ID in the mission graph

laneContent.description: This actor's experience at this node

model.description: Emotion model used. simple: existing -2 to +2 scale (default). dimensional: valence-arousal coordinates. categorical: discrete Plutchik primary emotion.

valence.description: Emotional valence from -1 (very negative) to +1 (very positive). Used with dimensional model.

arousal.description: Emotional arousal from 0 (calm) to 1 (highly activated). Used with dimensional model.

category.description: Plutchik primary emotion category. Used with categorical model.

emotions.description: This actor's emotional state. state and intensity are always valid (backward compatible). Optionally enrich with model, valence, arousal, or category for dimensional or categorical analysis.

barriers.description: Barriers as experienced by this actor (may differ from mission-level barriers)

emergesFrom.description: How this barrier emerges from this actor's traits colliding with the mission context

needAtStep.description: What this actor specifically needs at this step — emerges from combining the actor's traits/context with the mission's touchpoint. This is the micro-emergence: the specific, step-level need that only exists when THIS person meets THIS moment in the service.

painAtStep.description: How this step causes pain for this actor, beyond structural barriers. Captures the emotional and practical impact of unmet needs — the gap between what they need and what the service provides at this moment.

opportunities.description: Improvement opportunities specific to this actor's experience

cognitiveLoad.description: How this actor experiences the cognitive demands of this node, informed by WCAG 3.0 cognitive accessibility outcomes. Complements the service-level accessibilityProfile.cognitive on the Mission node — this captures what the actor actually encounters given their specific traits and context.

overallScore.description: Overall cognitive load rating from 1 (minimal) to 5 (overwhelming) as experienced by this actor

decisionComplexity.description: How complex the decisions feel to this actor at this node

informationDensity.description: How the volume and complexity of information is experienced by this actor

timePressure.description: Time pressure or urgency as felt by this actor

priorKnowledgeRequired.description: Domain knowledge this actor is expected to have — and whether they actually have it

supportAvailable.description: Help or scaffolding this actor can access to reduce cognitive load at this node

momentThatMatters.description: If this node is a critical emotional touchpoint for this actor

phases.description: Optional phase grouping for this experience. Can inherit from the mission's phases or define custom ones for this actor's view.

outcome.description: How this experience concludes for this actor

success.description: Did the actor achieve the mission goal?

reflection.description: Actor's overall reflection on the experience

wouldRepeat.description: Would this actor use the service again?

governance.description: Data classification and governance metadata. Supports GDPR Digital Omnibus and EU AI Act (Aug 2026) compliance. Distinct from provenance — governance covers classification and legal basis; provenance covers source and confidence.

dataClassification.description: Data sensitivity classification. public: no restrictions. internal: organisation only. confidential: need-to-know. restricted: regulatory controls apply.

containsPii.description: Whether this artifact contains or is derived from personally identifiable information.

piiCategories.description: Specific categories of PII present. Required when containsPii is true.

anonymisationMethod.description: How real data was anonymised. fictional_composite: persona is a fictional composite of multiple individuals. k_anonymity: data generalised so individuals cannot be distinguished. aggregated: only aggregate statistics used. differential_privacy: statistical noise added. none: no anonymisation applied.

retentionPolicy.description: Data retention policy reference or description (e.g., 'Retain for project duration + 12 months').

legalBasis.description: Legal basis for data processing under GDPR or equivalent (e.g., 'Legitimate interest — service improvement').

dataOwner.description: Person or team responsible for this data.

provenance.description: Evidence and confidence metadata. Can appear at artifact level or on any field via $provenance.

generationMethod.description: How this artifact was created. Supports EU AI Act Article 50 transparency requirements.

aiToolsUsed.description: AI tools used in creating this artifact. Supports EU AI Act Article 50 transparency requirements.

usage.description: What the tool was used for (e.g., 'initial draft generation', 'barrier analysis')

humanReviewed.description: Whether a human has reviewed the AI-generated content

humanReviewedDate.description: When the human review was completed

dataSourcesConsent.description: Whether consent was obtained for data sources used in AI generation

audience.description: Who this artifact is intended for

usageHints.description: Guidance for consumers on how to use this artifact
